metadata.description: Codebase-AI retrieval and agent benchmark questions: 18 on this project and 18 on julienschmidt/httprouter, both pinned by commit SHA in eval/config.json.
metadata.verification_note: IMPORTANT: You must manually verify every expected_file and expected_line_range against the pinned commit before trusting any baseline built on this dataset. Line ranges are checked for existence and bounds by `python -m eval.run --verify-dataset`, but their accuracy is a human responsibility.

questions.question: Where is the HTTP security chain configured so that only the auth and health endpoints are public?
reference_answer_points: The SecurityFilterChain bean is defined in SecurityConfig.java
Requests to /api/auth/** and /api/health are permitAll; every other request must be authenticated

questions.question: Where are the rate-limit ceilings for auth and AI endpoints defined, and what are they?
reference_answer_points: AUTH_LIMIT is 5 requests and AI_LIMIT is 20 requests per 60-second fixed window
The search and agent endpoints share the AI limit; login, register and resend-verification share the auth limit

questions.question: Where is the pgvector similarity query that backs semantic search?
reference_answer_points: CodeChunkRepository.findSimilarChunks is a native SQL query over the chunks table
It orders rows by the pgvector cosine-distance operator <=> and caps results with LIMIT :limit

questions.question: Where are the ZIP upload resource limits (per file and per archive) defined?
reference_answer_points: MAX_FILE_SIZE is 1 MB per extracted file and exceeding it aborts extraction
MAX_TOTAL_FILES caps the archive at 5000 files

questions.question: Where are the retrieval top-K defaults configured?
reference_answer_points: Retrieval.searchTopK defaults to 10 chunks and is what the search endpoint uses
Retrieval.chatTopK defaults to 5 chunks for chat context

questions.question: Where is the investigation agent's main tool-calling loop defined?
reference_answer_points: CodebaseAgent.investigate in ai-service/agent.py builds the prompt and runs the tool-calling loop
Its system prompt tells the model to cite specific files and line numbers and that it has a maximum of 10 tool calls

questions.question: How does the backend decide which requests require a verified email address?
reference_answer_points: Only POST requests are checked by the filter's requiresVerifiedUser method
Protected paths are project creation plus the upload/search/generated/sessions/agent sub-paths and session-message endpoints; plain GET reads stay open because they are ownership-checked

questions.question: How are email verification tokens created and delivered?
reference_answer_points: TOKEN_BYTES is 32 bytes from a SecureRandom
The emailed link points at {public-url}/auth/verify-email?token=<raw token>
Only a SHA-256 hash of the token is stored on the user row

questions.question: How does the AI service prevent embedding-dimension mismatches with the database?
reference_answer_points: EXPECTED_EMBEDDING_DIM is 384, matching the chunks.embedding vector(384) column
Startup raises RuntimeError when the configured model produces a different dimension
The model name comes from EMBEDDING_MODEL, defaulting to all-MiniLM-L6-v2

questions.question: How does the AI service authenticate server-to-server requests?
reference_answer_points: An HTTP middleware requires the X-Internal-Token header on every path except /health
A missing server-side token configuration returns 503 and a mismatched token returns 403 via constant-time compare_digest

questions.question: How does the storage layer block path traversal when reading project files?
reference_answer_points: normalize_relative_path rejects absolute paths (including Windows drive letters) and any '..' segment
LocalStorage.resolve additionally checks that the resolved path stays under the project root

questions.question: What happens when an unverified account tries to log in?
reference_answer_points: login throws 403 with the verification-required message before any token is minted
A wrong password is rejected as 401 invalid credentials before the verification check

questions.question: Trace the full path of a semantic search request from the HTTP endpoint down to pgvector and back.
reference_answer_points: POST /api/projects/{projectId}/search is handled by ProjectController.searchCode
ProjectService.searchCode embeds the question via AiServiceClient.generateEmbeddings before querying
Results come from CodeChunkRepository.findSimilarChunks ordered by cosine distance and are returned with filePath, startLine and endLine

questions.question: Trace how a single agent tool call flows from the LLM to the code and back.
reference_answer_points: The agent discovers tools from the MCP server's list_tools and keeps only read-only tools
_execute_tool overwrites any project_id chosen by the model with the investigation's project id
McpToolClient performs the HTTP call to the MCP server, whose registered handler executes the tool

questions.question: Trace what happens to an uploaded project ZIP from the HTTP request to a searchable index.
reference_answer_points: POST /{projectId}/upload calls ProjectService.uploadZip (processed synchronously at this commit)
uploadZip purges the previous index, extracts the staged ZIP with ZipExtractionService and stores each extracted file
CodeProcessingService.processProject chunks the stored files and embeds every chunk through the AI service

questions.question: Trace the account registration and email verification flow end to end.
reference_answer_points: POST /api/auth/register stores the user with verified=false and sends the mail inside the same transaction
EmailVerificationService.issueAndSend generates the raw token while only a hash is persisted
GET /api/auth/verify-email?token= consumes the single-use token and flips the account to verified

questions.question: Trace the checks a request must pass before the investigation agent runs for a project.
reference_answer_points: SecurityConfig requires authentication for every endpoint except /api/auth/** and /api/health
VerifiedUserFilter returns 403 for unverified users on agent endpoints
InMemoryRateLimitFilter caps agent requests at AI_LIMIT (20) per minute per user

questions.question: Trace what happens inside the AI service when a POST /chat request arrives.
reference_answer_points: The internal-token middleware runs first and rejects requests without a valid X-Internal-Token
The handler calls ChatService.generate_answer with the question, context and history
Citations in the response are built from the request's context entries, not produced by the model

questions.question: Where is httprouter's Router type defined and what does it hold?
reference_answer_points: type Router struct lives in router.go and stores the per-method route trees in trees map[string]*node
It also holds a sync.Pool of Params (paramsPool) for reuse across requests

questions.question: Where is the Router constructor and what behavior does it enable by default?
reference_answer_points: New() in router.go returns an initialized Router
It enables RedirectTrailingSlash, RedirectFixedPath, HandleMethodNotAllowed and HandleOPTIONS by default

questions.question: Where is route registration into the radix tree implemented?
reference_answer_points: (*node).addRoute in tree.go inserts a handle for a path into the tree
It delegates to insertChild to wire up leaf nodes and wildcard segments

questions.question: Where is the route lookup function that returns the handler, params and trailing-slash flag?
reference_answer_points: (*node).getValue in tree.go returns (handle, params, tsr)
The tsr flag signals that only the trailing-slash variant of the requested path exists

questions.question: Where does the router enter the http.Handler interface for an incoming request?
reference_answer_points: (*Router).ServeHTTP in router.go selects the tree for req.Method
It calls getValue with req.URL.Path and invokes the matched handler with the pooled params

questions.question: Where is request-path canonicalization implemented?
reference_answer_points: CleanPath in path.go returns a canonical slash path (an empty input becomes '/')
It collapses superfluous slashes and resolves . and .. segments while remembering a trailing slash

questions.question: How does the router handle a request whose only mismatch is a trailing slash?
reference_answer_points: getValue reports tsr=true and ServeHTTP redirects only when RedirectTrailingSlash is enabled
GET requests get 301 Moved Permanently while other methods get 308 Permanent Redirect
The path gains or loses exactly one trailing slash before the redirect

questions.question: How does the router answer OPTIONS requests automatically?
reference_answer_points: OPTIONS is auto-handled only when HandleOPTIONS is true and allowed() finds routes for the path
The Allow header is set from r.allowed(); a configured GlobalOPTIONS handler, if any, serves the body

questions.question: How does the router produce 405 Method Not Allowed?
reference_answer_points: With HandleMethodNotAllowed enabled, allowed() scans the other method trees for the same path
The Allow header lists the matching methods (plus OPTIONS) and a custom MethodNotAllowed handler overrides the default http.Error 405

questions.question: What does the router do when no route matches the request at all?
reference_answer_points: A configured NotFound handler serves the request when one is set
Otherwise the router falls back to http.NotFound, a plain 404

questions.question: How are named parameters and catch-all routes represented in the routing tree?
reference_answer_points: insertChild uses findWildcard to locate the wildcard segment and panics on malformed patterns (unnamed wildcards or conflicts with existing children)
A ':name' wildcard becomes a child node of type param and marks the parent's wildChild
Catch-all '*name' segments are processed by the same insertChild loop

questions.question: How does RedirectFixedPath rescue messy request paths such as //foo//bar or wrong casing?
reference_answer_points: ServeHTTP retries the lookup with CleanPath(path) through root.findCaseInsensitivePath when RedirectFixedPath is enabled
findCaseInsensitivePath is implemented recursively on the node type in tree.go
A successful fix issues the same 301/308 style redirect as the trailing-slash case

questions.question: Trace an incoming HTTP request from ServeHTTP to the final handler function.
reference_answer_points: ServeHTTP looks up r.trees[req.Method] and calls getValue(path)
On a match the handler runs with (w, req, params) and the params slice is returned to the pool via putParams
On a miss the router tries trailing-slash and fixed-path redirects, then OPTIONS/405 handling, then NotFound

questions.question: Trace how Router.GET('/path', handler) becomes a routable entry.
reference_answer_points: GET delegates to (*Router).Handle, which panics on an empty method, a path not starting with '/' or a nil handle
Handle stores the route in the tree for that method, creating r.trees[method] when it does not exist yet
The tree's addRoute splits static prefixes from wildcards via insertChild

questions.question: Trace what happens when a request misses a registered route only by a trailing slash.
reference_answer_points: getValue matches the slash variant and returns tsr=true instead of a handle
ServeHTTP issues the redirect when RedirectTrailingSlash is true, which New() sets by default
If the redirect option is disabled the request continues to fixed-path lookup and eventually NotFound

questions.question: Trace why a registered path returns 405 when called with the wrong HTTP method.
reference_answer_points: The lookup in the request method's tree fails (or that tree does not exist), so ServeHTTP falls through to r.allowed(path, method)
allowed() iterates the other method trees and collects every method whose getValue finds the path
A non-empty Allow list triggers the 405 branch when HandleMethodNotAllowed is true

questions.question: Where is the method that exposes routing decisions without writing a response?
reference_answer_points: (*Router).Lookup(method, path) in router.go returns (Handle, Params, bool)
It performs the same tree lookup as ServeHTTP but never writes to the ResponseWriter

questions.question: Where does the router manage its Params object pool?
reference_answer_points: getParams pulls a slice from r.paramsPool, a sync.Pool
putParams returns the slice after the handler finishes so params are reused across requests
